plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit all flagged positions (METU, MUU, SMCI) due to downtrends and below stop status.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet concentration limits and address the trim flag.
Reduce SMH to 5% to lower semiconductor exposure and address the trim flag.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged and underperforming assets. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and sell SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.

balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for ~2.5% monthly growth by blending broad index and quality tech. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a strong new setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL, METU, and MUU to increase leveraged and sector exposure.

aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets ~4% monthly growth by using and adding leveraged ETFs and concentrating in high-scoring setups. This strategy significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs, and maintain strict stop discipline to manage substantial loss risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MUU, SMCI) to zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce high-beta sector exposure.

income.read: This income-focused approach targets ~1% monthly yield by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure for lower drawdown. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
